open_obligations: Check that Hase et al.'s SGR uses training on hard data as the ceiling, so that exceeding it would break the metric
Check how often easy-only training actually exceeds full training in Sun et al.'s tables
out.other_title: Supervision Gap Recovered (SGR) metric for easy-to-hard generalization
out.rationale: The authors argue the SGR-style metric is limited in their setting because its ceiling can be exceeded, a critique of the metric's applicability without a direct conflict with Hase et al.'s findings, so CRITIQUES. Hase et al. study mostly multiple-choice tasks with ICL and SFT, not RL with reward models.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether a supervision-gap-recovered metric anchored on hard-data training is meaningful; holds where easy-only training can exceed the hard-data ceiling

text: The authors choose not to use an analogue of the easy-to-hard supervision gap recovered (SGR) metric of Hase et al. They say models trained only on easier tasks, particularly with RL, can outperform those trained on all difficulty levels, so they focus on absolute and relative performance on MATH500.
title: Sun et al. decline Hase et al.'s SGR metric because easy-only training can beat full training
